prompts.title: Recent form: wins, draws and losses
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16 composition on GoatLab charcoal #101412; the lower quarter is reserved throughout for permanent yellow Spanish subtitles, so every graphic element lives in the upper three quarters over a warm white #edf0e6 base, with lime #c5ed74 as the single accent and slate #8ca6bf for secondary text.

Editorial variant (approx. 6 s) — kinetic typography and rhythmic emphasis. The Spanish team names 'Real Betis Balompié' and 'FC Barcelona' enter as two stacked wordmarks, home in lime, away in slate, snapping in on separate beats with slight overshoot and motion blur. Three Spanish keywords — 'VICTORIAS', 'EMPATES', 'DERROTAS' — punch in as a vertical ladder in the centre of the upper half, each scaling from small to large and settling on its own rhythmic beat; the ladder then rearranges so the strongest beat lands on the largest word. No axes, no sample claims and no invented match events in this variant. Camera drifts upward by half a frame with slow parallax over a faint diagonal lime line; the focal point stays on the loudest keyword while the wordmarks hold steady at the top. A hard lime flash serves as the transition between keyword sets, and the block exits with a quick scale-down into the charcoal, handing over to the statistical presentation.

Statistical variant (approx. 9 s) — grouped horizontal count bars, three bars per team, home in lime, away in slate, ordered victorias, empates, derrotas, all measured against one shared zero baseline with a single 'partidos' unit axis drawn as thin warm white ticks. Spanish labels sit to the left of each group, and the values are rendered as {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}} for the home side and {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}} for the away side. Temporal staging: the home group grows from zero first, then the away group answers, each value counter rolling up beside its bar tip. A warm white sample badge below each team states the sample honestly — 'muestra {{home.n}}' and 'muestra {{away.n}}' — kept separate so that unequal samples would be visible at a glance, and a finer source line 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' sits at the foot of the graphic, clear of the subtitle band. The single focal point is the longest bar; all else sits at reduced opacity. Slow push-in on that bar during the main comparison, then a lime wipe transition into a held wide shot; exit by fading bars into outlines and cutting to charcoal.

prompts.title: Goals for and against
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16 frame on charcoal #101412 with the lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow Spanish subtitles; all illustration and charting stays in the upper three quarters, warm white #edf0e6 for structure, lime #c5ed74 for the home side, slate #8ca6bf for the away side.

Editorial variant (approx. 7 s) — illustrative football pitch and ball path. A stylised pitch drawn in thin warm white lines sits in the upper half at a slight perspective tilt, with the two goals glowing softly: the home end rimmed in lime, the away end rimmed in slate. Spanish team names appear as goal-mouth labels, 'Real Betis Balompié' at the lower edge of the pitch and 'FC Barcelona' at the upper edge, settling into place with a gentle drop and blur-out. A single lime ball travels along an arcing path from the halfway circle toward one goal, trailing a faint light streak; on contact the net ripples as wireframe lines and the Spanish heading 'GOLES A FAVOR' pulses once. A second ball path, this time in slate, mirrors the movement toward the opposite goal under the heading 'GOLES RECIBIDOS'. No numbers, no axes, no sample claims, no invented scorers or match events in this variant. Camera follows the ball with a whip pan and a slight handheld sway, then eases back to frame the whole pitch. A lime flash is the transition between the two ball paths; the exit tilts the pitch away and dissolves it into charcoal.

Statistical variant (approx. 8 s) — four paired bars laid out as two small multiples: one column headed 'Goles a favor' and one headed 'Goles recibidos', each with a home bar in lime and an away bar in slate, all four on one shared zero baseline with the unit 'goles' written on the warm white axis. Values are rendered as {{home.gf}}, {{away.gf}}, {{home.ga}} and {{away.ga}}. Spanish labels 'Real Betis Balompié' and 'FC Barcelona' label each pair. Bars grow upward from zero with a counter roll, attacking pair first, conceding pair second, so the temporal stages read cleanly. Sample and source annotation runs in warm white micro-type beneath the chart: 'muestra {{home.n}} partidos' for the home side, 'muestra {{away.n}} partidos' for the away side, plus 'Fuente: Bzzoiro'. The focal point is the tallest attacking bar; the remaining three step back in opacity during the main comparison. A slow vertical push-in holds on that bar, a lime wipe transition carries into the frozen comparison, and the exit fades every bar to a zero-height outline before cutting to charcoal.

prompts.title: Clean sheets compared with their samples
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16 canvas on charcoal #101412. The lower quarter stays clear for permanent yellow Spanish subtitles; every defensive graphic lives in the upper three quarters, using warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf.

Editorial variant (approx. 6 s) — defensive energy and a stylised shield. A large shield outline in warm white is drawn stroke by stroke in the centre of the frame and then fills with a slow lime gradient rising from its base; slate is used only for the away-side accents so the two sides never blur together. The Spanish heading 'ARCO EN CERO' snaps in above the shield in condensed uppercase, while the Spanish team names 'Real Betis Balompié' and 'FC Barcelona' rotate in as opposing tabs on either side, home tab lime, away tab slate. Rhythmic impacts send thin concentric lime shockwaves out from the shield on each beat, and a goalkeeper-glove silhouette briefly stamps the surface as pure graphic texture, without any invented save or match event. No axes, no counts and no sample claims in this variant. Camera pushes in slowly, then drifts sideways to reveal the second tab, with focus breathing between shield and heading. A lime shutter is the transition that swaps the tabs; the exit collapses the shield into a single thin line that drops toward the subtitle band.

Statistical variant (approx. 9 s) — counts compared directly, without converting anything into rates. Two horizontal bars, home in lime and away in slate, share one zero baseline with the unit 'partidos' written on the warm white axis, annotated with {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}}. Spanish labels 'Arcos en cero' plus the Spanish team names sit to the left. Because a bare count says little on its own, an explicit sample ribbon in warm white micro-type runs beneath the bars: 'muestra {{home.n}} partidos' and 'muestra {{away.n}} partidos', with the source credit 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' pinned at the right edge of the ribbon. Entry: bars extend from zero with rolling counters, then the ribbon slides in from the left as a bar-wide underline. The main comparison is the pair of bar lengths; emphasis is a soft lime glow on the longer bar while the other recedes in opacity. Camera holds a slow push-in with no rotation. Exit: values and ribbon fade first, bars retract into outlines, then a lime wipe transition returns the frame to charcoal.

prompts.title: Head-to-head history, not a forecast
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16, charcoal #101412 base, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf as the two side colours; the lower quarter stays reserved for permanent yellow Spanish subtitles.

Editorial variant (approx. 7 s) — both teams as a visual duel. The frame splits vertically into two facing panels, the left rimmed in lime and the right rimmed in slate, each dark enough to keep the Spanish subtitles legible. The Spanish team names 'Real Betis Balompié' and 'FC Barcelona' rise from the bottom corners as bold wordmarks and lock into place, then the Spanish heading 'HISTORIAL DE CRUCES' is stamped across the top in condensed uppercase. A thin warm white seam runs down the middle and pulses like a heartbeat; each pulse sends a lime shockwave from the home panel and a slate one from the away panel, meeting at the seam and cancelling there. No counts, no axes, no forecast and no invented match events in this variant. Camera dollies slowly toward the seam, then racks focus so one panel steps forward as the momentary focal point. A whip-pan is the transition that flips the composition; the exit wipes both panels into the seam, leaving one line that fades to charcoal.

Statistical variant (approx. 9 s) — one stacked count bar divided into three segments: lime for 'Victorias Real Betis Balompié' {{h2h.homeWins}}, slate for 'Victorias FC Barcelona' {{h2h.awayWins}} and warm white for 'Empates' {{h2h.draws}}, all measured against one shared zero baseline with the unit 'partidos' shown as ticks on the warm white axis. The total is stated honestly beside the bar as 'cruces previos {{h2h.total}}', accompanied by the sample note 'muestra {{h2h.total}} partidos' and the source line 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' along the foot of the graphic. Segments resolve in sequence from the left with counters rolling at each boundary, and each divider flashes lime as it locks. The focal point is the widest segment; the others step back in opacity while it holds. A restrained Spanish disclaimer sits in micro-type just above the subtitle band: 'Datos históricos, no un pronóstico.' Camera pushes in gently on the boundary between the two win segments, holds, then eases out. Exit: the bar contracts into the centre, the disclaimer fades last, and a soft lime transition returns to charcoal.

prompts.title: Grounded synthesis of available facts
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16 on charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6 type, lime #c5ed74 for the home side and slate #8ca6bf for the away side; the lower quarter is permanently reserved for yellow Spanish subtitles.

Editorial variant (approx. 7 s) — team reveals and narrative emphasis. Two vertical light curtains, lime on the left and slate on the right, sweep in from opposite edges and part to reveal the Spanish team names 'Real Betis Balompié' and 'FC Barcelona' stacked over a faint pitch texture. A single Spanish headline locks between them — 'DOS MOMENTOS, UN CRUCE' — and its accent word scales up on the narration stress, while short Spanish phrases drawn from the spoken line slide in beneath each name and are emphasised rhythmically. No axes, no counts, no derived metrics and no invented match events in this variant. Camera glides upward through the parting curtains, then settles with a subtle parallax between the two names. A lime flash is the transition from the home reveal to the away reveal; the exit closes both curtains inward over the charcoal and clears the frame for subtitles.

Statistical variant (approx. 9 s) — a compact summary of compatible available facts only, with no estimates and no predictions. Two mirrored groups of three short bars — 'Victorias', 'Empates', 'Derrotas' — sit either side of a central warm white divider, home bars lime, away bars slate, each group on its own shared zero baseline but drawn at the identical scale, with the unit 'partidos' labelled on both warm white axes so the comparison stays unit-consistent. Values render as {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}} and {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Below, a slim goal-output strip shows {{home.gf}} and {{away.gf}} under the Spanish label 'Goles a favor'. Sample and source treatment appear in warm white micro-type: 'muestra' badges for each recent sample using {{home.n}} and {{away.n}}, a 'Fuente: Bzzoiro' credit, plus the Spanish disclaimer 'Solo datos publicados, sin pronóstico.' Entry is staggered — home group grows, away group answers, goal strip wipes in last — and the focal point is whichever win bar resolves longest, with everything else dimmed slightly during the main comparison. Camera eases in and holds. Exit fades the strip, retracts all bars to zero and finishes with a lime wipe transition to charcoal.
